newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: India, Sri Lanka to hold talks on shipping.
newsitem.headline: India, Sri Lanka to hold talks on shipping.

text.p: An Indian delegation will arrive in Sri Lanka soon to discuss alternative ports of call for small Indian vessels from southern India's Tuticorin, Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar said on Wednesday.

The port of Colombo, citing security reasons, last month banned the entry of Indian vessels below 3,000 tonnes. The ban mainly affected vessels from Tuticorin, which were diverted to the southern Sri Lankan port of Galle.

Sri Lanka lifted the ban on January 4, Kadirgamar told a news conference at the end of a four-day visit by Indian External Affairs Minister Inder Kumar Gujral. But Sri Lankan officials said the government was trying to discourage Tuticorin vessels from using Colombo harbour.
Sri Lankan navy officials said the ban was imposed because of intelligence that Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam could attack the port, using Tuticorin vessels as cover.
The rebels staged an abortive suicide attack on Colombo port in April 1996.
